assessment.transport_assessment: One submission acknowledged a response ID; 78 GET polls of the same ID observed queued, in_progress and incomplete. All 79 HTTP operations returned 200. The 174.409-second generation exceeded the former synchronous connection wait while staying within the unchanged 360-second review scheduling budget. No transport timeout or cancellation occurred; the job was already terminal.
assessment.budget_assessment: The first scope pass returned max_output_tokens after using all 6,000 output tokens as reasoning tokens. No review passed response/evidence validation. The reviewer stopped with response_incomplete before any domain or challenge generation. Returned usage is known and counted once despite duplicate terminal accounting in attempts and calls.
assessment.quality_assessment: No accepted review exists, so source correctness, appropriate core-dependency scope and semantic quality remain unassessed for this comparison. This is a transport-observability success and a generation-budget failure, not a review-quality pass.
assessment.causal_limit: Source snapshot identity matches the last synchronous failure, but the policy also changed and service conditions differ. This run does not establish the cause of earlier requests with no response metadata. One completed transport trial does not establish production reliability.
assessment.next_action: Preserve this failure and stop the predeclared live series. Design a separate representative budget calibration with explicit per-pass/overall generation, time and spend constraints before further live audits. Do not silently trim source, substitute models, accept truncation or retry until success.
assessment.hardware_boundary: No candidate code, QEMU test or physical device operation was performed by Astra. The implementation PR has separate deterministic CI/QEMU evidence.
